steps.title: Assemble Dual Breathing Circuit
steps.instruction: Connect all components of the dual‑breathing circuit and gas supply according to the manufacturer diagrams.

substeps.instruction: Insert the clear fitting on the semi‑transparent feed‑tube of the Dual Breathing Circuit into one Induction Chamber port; connect one end of a 22 mm FlexHose to the other Induction Chamber port and the opposite end of the FlexHose to a Charcoal Filter (FlexHose may be cut at the ridge in the smooth junctions).
Attach the second Charcoal Filter to the free end of the 22 mm FlexHose at the end of the Patient Breathing Circuit.
Insert a 9 mm, 12 mm or 14 mm nose cone into the Patient Breathing Circuit elbow fitting.
Insert the blue connector (black tubing) of the Dual Breathing Circuit into the Common Outlet of the anesthesia machine (Table‑Top or Mobile model).

Connect the gas‑supply hose assembly to the rear inlet DISS fitting of the machine; tighten gently with an 11/16 in wrench on the hose fitting and a 5/8 in wrench on the DISS inlet fitting. Connect the opposite end of the DISS hose to the tank‑mounted regulator or in‑house O₂ line set to a maximum operating pressure of 55 PSI (pressures >55 PSI may damage the system).

steps.title: Perform Pre‑Operative System Check
steps.instruction: Verify gas connections, flowmeter operation, flush valve function, leak‑tightness, and vaporizer fill before starting anesthesia.

substeps.instruction: Attach each gas supply line to its appropriate D.I.S.S. inlet on the back of the flowmeter(s) and connect any additional supply hoses as needed.

Turn on the gas supply and confirm sufficient quantity for the planned procedures; when turning off a flowmeter, rotate the control knob clockwise only until the ball float reaches the bottom of the tube (do not over‑tighten).
Test the oxygen flowmeter through its full range by turning the control knob counter‑clockwise to open and clockwise to close; close the valve when the test is complete.

Test the oxygen flush valve by depressing and holding the button for 3 seconds – oxygen should flush rapidly from the common outlet and stop immediately when the button is released; if the button does not return to OFF or flow does not stop, remove the machine from service and have the valve repaired by VetEquip or an authorized service facility.
For Model 901809, perform the “10 Second Leak Test” as described in the manual to confirm the breathing circuit is leak‑free.
Fill the vaporizer with the appropriate anesthetic agent according to the vaporizer instruction manual.

steps.title: Prime System and Verify Leaks
steps.instruction: Assemble the full anesthesia circuit, check for leaks, and prepare the vaporizer before placing animals.

substeps.instruction: Open the oxygen tank (or verify in‑house supply) and ensure regulator pressure is within the 55 PSI limit; if hissing is heard, inspect and tighten the gasket between tank and regulator (E‑cylinder only).
Connect the machine to the dual‑delivery system at the common outlet (friction‑fit) and verify a leak‑free seal.
Connect the dual‑delivery system to the nose‑cone and induction‑chamber fittings (friction‑fit) and verify leak‑free seals.

Attach the breathing‑elbow down‑tube and chamber outlet port to the charcoal filters; ensure each filter is oriented vertically with the exit holes at the bottom unobstructed and secured in the provided canister holder.
NOTE: The induction chamber is airtight – if the oxygen flowmeter is turned off, no airflow will enter the chamber. Never leave animals in the chamber without oxygen flow.
WARNING: Do not place charcoal filters directly on a surface; use the holder to avoid back‑pressure.
If required, fill the vaporizer with the appropriate liquid anesthetic agent per the vaporizer manual.
Open the stopcock in the chamber‑tubing line and close the stopcock in the nose‑cone line.
Set the oxygen flowmeter to at least 1 L min⁻¹.
Place the first animal in the induction chamber and secure the lid (multiple animals may be placed if they fit comfortably).

steps.title: Induce Anesthesia in First Animal
steps.instruction: Deliver anesthetic vapor and evacuate induction chamber to achieve loss of consciousness.

substeps.instruction: Turn the vaporizer dial to 2‑2.5 % (2‑2½ %). The animal should lose consciousness within ~2 minutes.

When the animal shows no response to rocking/jiggling, press the oxygen flush button for 20‑30 seconds (for a 2 L chamber) to evacuate anesthesia‑saturated gas; ensure the nose‑cone stopcock remains closed to prevent pressure‑driven ejection of the animal’s nose.
Open the stopcock in the nose‑cone line.
Immediately close the stopcock in the chamber‑tubing line, open the chamber lid, and remove the animal from the induction chamber.
Place the animal’s nose into the nose cone.

steps.title: Repeat for Additional Animals
steps.instruction: Cycle subsequent animals through induction, then transition them to the nose cone while completing procedures on the first animal.

substeps.instruction: Place the next animal in the induction chamber and open the chamber‑tubing stopcock.
When the procedure on the previous animal is finished, close the nose‑cone stopcock and move that animal to a recovery unit (awakening occurs in ~2 minutes).
Repeat the induction‑flush‑transfer steps (steps 7‑11 of the protocol) for each additional animal until all are processed.

steps.title: Shut Down and Clean Equipment
steps.instruction: Turn off all gas flows, power down the system, and sanitize reusable components.

substeps.instruction: Turn the vaporizer dial to the OFF position.
Turn off the oxygen flowmeter.
If a freestanding oxygen tank is used, close the tank valve.

Clean and sanitize the induction chamber, nose cone, and any other reusable parts according to your facility’s cleaning protocols (avoid petroleum‑based lubricants; use silicone‑based lubricants only if lubrication is required).
